key_insight: In Alzheimer’s MRI, deep-learning PVS segmentation models can score well yet still fail to preserve biologically meaningful associations, so accuracy alone is not enough.
clinical_relevance: Before using automated PVS measures for research or clinical inference in AD, models should be validated on the target cohort to ensure they reproduce known biomarker relationships.
method: Benchmarked 5 open-source nnU-Net-based PVS segmentation models.
Compared outputs against manual labels in 60 multi-site ADNI-3 participants and 12 external VALDO scans.
Tested segmentation performance and whether model-derived PVS burden matched ground-truth biomarker associations.
evidence_signal: The AD-trained ADNI-PVS-Net had the best internal Dice (0.58±0.14) but dropped to ≤0.11 externally, while other models generalized better externally (0.27–0.30) yet often failed to reproduce the expected PVS–amyloid association.
watch_item: External generalizability and downstream biological validity can diverge, and some models misclassified up to 32% of white matter hyperintensities as PVS.
paper_title: Examining the Clinical Utility of Deep Learning Models for Perivascular Space Segmentation in Alzheimer's Disease
